WEG.why: makes power and distribution transformers and substations for T&D grid build-outs (capacity being roughly doubled in Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and the U.S.) plus Marathon alternators for data-center energy backup; data-center and grid demand drives its GTD orders
WEG.evidence: WEG Q2 FY2026 call (07-23-2026): finance & IR officer - exposure to data centers through Marathon alternators for energy backup and transformers used in the connection of data centers or grids; T&D capacity expansion of practically 100% versus 2023-2024

players.product: Power and distribution transformers and substations (T&D) for grid connection, plus Marathon alternators for data-center energy backup and industrial pumps / ventilation equipment for cooling systems

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 (VP Finance Andre Luis Rodrigues): net operating revenue decreased 0.6% versus Q2 2025, as the absence of centralized solar generation deliveries in Brazil and BRL appreciation were virtually neutralized by continued growth abroad; EBITDA BRL 2.2 billion, down 2.1%, with an EBITDA margin of 21.8% despite higher raw material costs, U.S. import tariffs and personnel expenses tied to capacity expansion; ROIC up 0.7 percentage points to 33.6%. The external market grew 11.8% in local currency and 14.7% in USD.
quarterly_data.figure: net operating revenue -0.6% YoY; EBITDA BRL 2.2 billion (-2.1%), margin 21.8%; external market +11.8% local currency / +14.7% USD

quarterly_data.signal: Management (Andre Menegueti Salgueiro): in the external market the T&D business presented another quarter with a good volume of deliveries tied to strengthening electrical grid infrastructure in the United States, the Marathon generator business in the U.S. continues to perform well, and short-cycle demand was strong in the U.S. and Europe, especially oil and gas and ventilation and cooling systems for data centers; in Brazil GTD revenue is still hit by the lack of centralized solar projects while deliveries of large transformers and substations continue. Short cycle was 61% and long cycle 39% of Q2 revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: short cycle 61% / long cycle 39% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Transformer capacity ramp (Salgueiro): WEG announced a T&D capacity expansion of practically 100% versus 2023 and 2024; 10% was already added, the anticipated Betim expansion adds another 10 to 15% in the middle of the year (about 25% of the announced capacity), and the other 75% becomes operational at the beginning of next year with new factories in Mexico and Colombia. The dates are when factories are ready, not full output; along 2027 and especially 2028 the factories are expected to run at optimized capacity and profitability similar to current T&D operations. Personnel expenses rose because people are hired and trained before transformer production starts.
quarterly_data.figure: T&D capacity +~100% vs 2023-2024; Betim +10-15% mid-2026 (25% of announced capacity); remaining 75% beginning of next year (Mexico, Colombia)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex (management): the 2026 capital budget of BRL 3.6 billion is still valid; BRL 1.4 billion was completed in the first half and spending is concentrated in the second half. Q2 investments totaled BRL 795 million, 45% in Brazil and 55% abroad, including transformer factories in Mexico, Colombia and the U.S., T&D capacity in Brazil and high-voltage equipment capacity in China.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex budget BRL 3.6 billion; H1 BRL 1.4 billion; Q2 BRL 795 million

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (Rodrigues): demand remains positive abroad, with strong orders for long-cycle equipment in both industrial and T&D; management is confident of a return of revenue growth for the remainder of the year, helped by normalization of the 2025 comparison base. International growth in H1 was in line with the initial expectation of about two digits, but the appreciated BRL will generate less growth in BRL than expected at the start of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: international growth of about two digits

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers (Salgueiro): WEG's data-center exposure is mainly Marathon alternators for energy backup, transformers used in the connection of data centers or grids, and growing demand for pumps and ventilation for cooling refrigeration systems; WEG does not sell directly to data centers but sees very positive demand. Solid-state transformers inside data centers are monitored but still being developed and not at commercial scale; no significant change expected for grid and connection equipment.

Orders and pricing (management): the industry is 'very heated' with high demand, seen in backlog and order intake especially in GTD, including T&D and Marathon alternators. Rodrigues: demand for transformers in North America is unchanged; pricing is set project by project with parametric formulas on copper and steel, and the current pricing level in the sector is 'still very attractive', though price growth is lower than in the past.

Tariffs (Rodrigues): Section 301 tariffs of 25% took effect on July 22; Section 232 applies to large transformers from Mexico at 50% above 10 MVA and 25% below; a cumulative application could reach 37%. Of WEG's U.S. revenue, 33% is produced in the U.S., about 20% is exported from Brazil (about 30% in 2024), 41% is produced in Mexico and 4% elsewhere. Tariff pass-through clauses on transformer contracts are expected to continue this year and into the beginning of next year.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. revenue sourcing: 33% U.S., ~20% Brazil, 41% Mexico, 4% other

quarterly_data.signal: Battery storage (management): WEG has 1 gigawatt of capacity split between mobility and BESS; the new Itajai factory, to be completed next year, will add 2 gigawatts.
quarterly_data.figure: BESS/mobility capacity 1 GW; +2 GW from Itajai factory
